ledger.x: 100 BCE: Teotihuacan is established in the northeastern Basin of Mexico.
50 BCE: Teotihuacan comes to dominate the valley around the city.
c. 150–200: Cuicuilco is abandoned after Xitle's eruption and its people disperse 'toward Toluca and Teotihuacan'. The Cuicuilco page's dates conflict; 200 is the end of…
378: Siyaj K'ak' arrives at Tikal and a Teotihuacan-backed dynasty takes the throne.

c. 426 (bridging): the Teotihuacan-installed line at Tikal is 'rapidly Mayanized' ('Although the new rulers of Tikal were foreign, their descendants were rapidly Mayanized'). The Tikal page says Yax Nuun Ahiin I 'reigned for 47 years as king of Tikal, and remained a vassal of Siyaj K'ak' for as long as the latter…
650: Teotihuacan's hold on the Basin of Mexico lapses as Period IV begins.
705: the city's neighbourhood falls away and only the city itself is drawn to its end.

wars.name: Teotihuacan entrada at Tikal
wars.outcome: Siyaj K'ak', 'probably a foreign general', arrives at Tikal on 14 January 378 as Chak Tok Ich'aak dies; Yax Nuun Ahiin I, son of Spearthrower Owl, is enthroned on 13 September 379 and Siyaj K'ak' becomes king at Uaxactun.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines: the basin frontier is the researcher's reading of the page; the Petén sphere is a client relation, not a border.
